reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses DSC melting measurements of small organic molecules, irrelevant to HEAs. E2 mentions CALPHAD modeling for rare earth sesquioxides, not HEAs or third-generation models with short-range order. E3 reviews thermodynamic properties of pure Cr and V, mentioning thermal vacancies but not HEAs or the integrated DSC-CALPHAD approach. No cited passage provides evidence for the claimed accuracy, the synergy, or the baseline error comparison.
premises: High-throughput DSC can provide precise heat capacity curves near melting for HEAs, yielding enthalpy and entropy of fusion via integration.
Third-generation CALPHAD models can account for thermal vacancy effects and deviations from random solid-solution behavior (e.g., short-range order) in HEAs.
Combining DSC and CALPHAD can predict liquid-phase thermodynamics and volume change at melting for HEAs.
The integrated approach will achieve ±2–5% accuracy for melting temperature, latent heat, entropy of fusion, and volume change across diverse HEAs.
Traditional methods (rule-of-mixture or second-generation CALPHAD) show larger errors (≈10% or more) for HEA melting predictions.
